findings.text: Printk services expose a timed flush operation scoped to one console or to all consoles and a dump notification dispatcher. The flush captures the current log reservation point, triggers pending output for atomic and legacy paths, then polls until every usable consumer has advanced past that point or the budget expires. The dispatcher walks registered dump handlers and invokes those whose configured severity threshold admits the current cause.

Watchdog services expose two small notrace touch operations. One refreshes the scheduler soft lockup report deadline on the calling processor using a raw per-CPU write, tolerating enabled preemption. The other performs that refresh and additionally pokes the workqueue watchdog for the current processor.

Audit record construction uses allocation and release helpers around a cache object holding a queue of message fragments plus a current fragment, owning context reference, allocation mode, and timestamp. Allocation creates the object, attaches an initial message buffer, and reserves header space, unwinding cleanly on failure. Release drains queued fragments and returns the object. Growth extends current tail capacity and accounts size, reporting loss on exhaustion.

Audit emission offers start, formatted append, session annotation, subject annotation, and completion. Start validates global initialization and exclusion policy, enforces backlog admission with optional waiting, stamps and labels the record. Append safely ignores absent buffers and expands storage as needed. Completion subjects each fragment to rate admission before handing to the global queue, otherwise recording loss, then wakes the delivery thread.

Audit filtering evaluates ordered rules under read-side protection. Each rule requires all its field predicates to succeed, covering process identity, message category, login identity, executable origin via filesystem mark comparison, and access control attributes. A matching terminal rule suppresses auditing or stops further evaluation. Field comparison supports equality families, ordered relations, and bit tests for numeric values, with identity-aware variants for user and group identifiers.

Audit configuration exposes setters for message rate, queue depth, wait budget, enablement state, and failure disposition. All funnel through a shared change helper that records a configuration event when active, honors a locked enablement state by denying updates with a permission failure, and applies the new value only when permitted. Enablement additionally latches a sticky ever-enabled flag. A separate connection setter installs daemon identity with reference-counted process and network references and deferred reclamation.

Delivery helpers implement printk fallback and queue placement for records that cannot be sent immediately. One helper emits a one-line notice for non-terminator messages under printk rate control. Others place records onto hold or retry queues when limits allow, otherwise emit via printk and account loss. Retry placement is used for transient send failures while hold placement preserves records when the consumer has disappeared, subject to a global default-drop policy.

Message admission is throttled to a configured count per timer tick window using protected counters and a last-reset timestamp; a zero limit disables throttling. Lost-event accounting increments a global loss counter and warns at most once per window unless configured for panic or unthrottled operation, and always invokes the configured failure action.

Record stamps combine a coarse wall-clock reading with a monotonically increasing atomic serial. When a syscall context supplies a valid stamp it is reused and the context is promoted to recording priority on first use; otherwise a fresh clock plus serial pair is generated. A build without syscall auditing always reports absence, forcing fresh generation.

Backlog admission waits or drops only for ordinary producers. Records generated by the collection daemon itself or by a holder of the control mutex bypass queue-depth blocking to avoid deadlock, with the latter penalized later on a safe path. Ordinary producers with blocking-capable allocation may sleep in exclusive wait with a bounded budget while the delivery thread is signaled; non-blocking or budget-exhausted producers record loss and abandon the record.

Dump delivery defaults an unset per-client threshold to a mid-severity oops level, or to maximum verbosity when a global always-dump flag is set. Clients whose threshold is below the current cause are skipped without invocation.

Executable-based filtering applies only to the current task with live address space and a resolvable executable file. Identity is the pair of inode number and device number compared against a stored mark; an unset mark never matches. Builds without filesystem notification support provide constant fallbacks that reject or disable matching.

Filter evaluation and dump dispatch run under read-side critical sections without sleeping or mutation. Rate and loss throttles serialize short counter and timestamp updates with interrupt-safe spin protection using dedicated static locks. Daemon connection replacement holds an interrupt-safe spinlock while swapping the protected pointer and defers freeing of the old object to a grace period with reference drops.

Flush polling serializes access to legacy consumer progress with the global console lock while iterating consoles under a source-visibility read guard, deliberately retaining the lock even when no legacy consumers exist to cover concurrent registration. Each unlock pass also advances pending legacy output. Sequence reads use an atomic-path accessor for non-blocking consoles and direct progress fields otherwise.

Observed usage implies a record buffer carrying a list of message fragments, a pointer to the active fragment, owning audit context, allocation mode, and stamp with seconds, sub-second fraction, and serial. Dump detail carries a cause enumeration and description pointer. Flush type carries separate indicators for atomic and legacy direct paths. Daemon connection carries process reference, port identifier, network reference, and reclamation linkage.

Flush progresses through early rejection when scheduling is unavailable, reservation capture, initial kick of pending output, then a repeating observe-decide-wait cycle. Observation sums remaining distance across usable consumers. Decision resets the remaining budget on progress when requested, succeeds when no distance remains, and fails on budget exhaustion. Waiting sleeps briefly while measuring elapsed ticks to tolerate oversleep.

Per-fragment completion first passes rate admission; admitted fragments join the main queue while rejected ones are discarded with loss accounting. Failed sends enter hold or retry placement: transient failures prefer the retry queue, permanent absence prefers the hold queue, each bounded by the backlog limit with printk fallback and loss on overflow. A dedicated rehold path unconditionally returns a fragment to the hold queue.

Callable entry points include the timed flush waiter that reports full consumption, the dump dispatcher invoked on fault or shutdown causes, the soft lockup touch helpers callable from atomic or notrace contexts, and the audit start-format-end family plus filter and comparator predicates. All tolerate defined no-op conditions such as absent buffers, uninitialized auditing, or excluded message types by returning neutral values.

Flush must not be invoked before scheduling is active and may sleep during polling; measuring by ticks avoids dependence on precise sleep duration. Audit growth and allocation failures must record loss rather than stall. Aux record creation can fail for memory, in which case callers restore the prior active fragment and propagate an out-of-memory status. Multi-provider security labeling emits a placeholder in the primary record and an auxiliary record, tolerating unsupported providers.

Configuration changes are denied when global enablement is in the locked state, and enablement values beyond the locked sentinel or failure modes outside the three defined dispositions are rejected as invalid. Denied attempts still generate a configuration record when auditing is active, with a result field reflecting denial.
